description: Decode attention (one query token per sequence, or a few for MTP verify when q_len > 1 is a separate case) over a paged KV cache with GQA: aiter paged_attention / pa_fwd, vLLM/sglang paged decode, MLA decode over a dense latent cache.

max_context.doc: longest sequence in the case; seq_lens are drawn up to it

num_blocks.doc: pool blocks allocated in the case (>= batch * max_blocks)

hooks.kv_cache_layout: (t, name, sym) -> the cache in the layout the kernel reads (aiter's [blocks, kv_heads, head_size/x, block_size, x] key and [blocks, kv_heads, head_size, block_size] value layouts, vLLM's, or row-major). The logical cache stays [blocks, block_size, kv_heads, head_size]. fp8 caches: apply the deployment's k_scale/v_scale and add them as scalar inputs (override) when the kernel takes them.

call: Invoke the decode entry with the deployment's arguments (max_seq_len / partition sizes as the server computes them) and return out.

timing.cache: the KV pool is long-lived and much larger than L2 at serving context lengths; read-evict matches. Draw seq_lens from the observed per-request contexts (override dist) for timing buckets: uniform lengths up to max_context halve the mean work.

negative_controls: read block_table[b][i + 1] for the last block: the tail of every multi-block sequence attends to wrong keys
omit the scale multiply: softmax sharpens, error ~|out|
pitfalls: The partition (split-K) count depends on max_seq_len and batch; replay sigs must span the partition ladder, and a static graph buffer sized for the largest case must be correct for smaller ones (the OOB-under-replay failure mode).
A contiguous block_table hides indexing bugs and is faster than a fragmented pool; page_table draws a shuffled pool.
Allocate num_blocks for the case, not for the largest case: the touched set, not the pool size, sets cache residency.
